title: Annotatio III §.VII (1): Careful weighing of disputed dogmas; consensus and dissent marked without varnish; modest judgment on weight more than bare truth — consciences unhurt
pass_a_gloss: (1.) That it carefully weighed the moments of the special disputed Dogmas, annotated Consensus and Dissensus everywhere without varnish, and only then rendered a modest judgment concerning the Weight of Consensus and Dissensus more than concerning Truth, with consciences on both sides unhurt.
pass_b_english: (1.) It carefully weighed the force of the special disputed doctrines, marked consensus and dissent everywhere without varnish,
and only then gave a modest judgment on the weight of that consensus and dissent more than on bare truth — leaving both sides’ consciences unhurt.
source_text: (1.) Quòd specialium Dogmatum controversorum momenta accuratè expenderit, Consensum Dissensumque ubique, citra fucum, annotaverit, & tum demum de Consensûs Dissensûsque Pondere magis, quàm Veritate, modestum judicium, illaesis utrinque Conscienciis, tulerit.

lemmas.gloss: by weight more than by truth

notes: Cassellanum mark (1): accurate expendere; citra fucum; Pondus magis quam Veritas; illaesis Conscienciis.
